channel.title: Nature Materials
channel.description: Nature Materials is a multidisciplinary journal aimed at bringing together cutting-edge research across the entire spectrum of materials science and technology. Nature Materials covers all applied and fundamental aspects of the synthesis/processing, structure/composition, properties and performance of materials. Nature Materials provides a forum for the development of a common identity among materials scientists while encouraging researchers to cross established subdisciplinary lines. To achieve this, Nature Materials takes an interdisciplinary, integrated and balanced approach to all areas of materials research while fostering the exchange of ideas between scientists involved in different communities.

item.title: [8] Probing the quantum metric of 3D topological insulators
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Carmine Ortix, Andrea D. Caviglia

Authors: Giacomo Sala, Emanuele Longo, Maria Teresa Mercaldo, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Important experimental transport study on topological insulators relevant to band structure studies.

Tags: #topologicalinsulator #quantummetric #transport

Abstract: Nature Materials, Published online: 22 May 2026; doi:10.1038/s41563-026-02617-3 The quantum metric of a surface Dirac cone is found to contribute to the nonlinear magnetoresistance of thin films of the 3D topological insulator Sb2Te3.

item.title: [7] Layer photovoltaic effect in a two-dimensional antiferromagnet with parity–time symmetry
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Yoshihiro Iwasa, Toshiya Ideue

Authors: Yu Dong, Sota Kitamura, Yuki M. Itahashi, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of magnetic order and symmetry in 2D materials relevant to the user.

Tags: #antiferromagnet #2Dmaterials #magnetism

Abstract: Nature Materials, Published online: 18 May 2026; doi:10.1038/s41563-026-02593-8 A layer-dependent photocurrent is demonstrated in bilayer CrSBr, and it can be directly controlled by the magnetic configuration.

item.title: [6] All-optical control of antiferromagnetic domains via an inverse optical magnetoelectric effect
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Y. Tokura, N. Ogawa

Authors: S. Toyoda, V. Kocsis, Y. Tokunaga, et al.

Score 6/10 C_MAYBE

Why: Optical control of magnetic domains is relevant to experimental condensed matter magnetism.

Tags: #antiferromagnet #optics #magnetism

Abstract: Nature Materials, Published online: 15 May 2026; doi:10.1038/s41563-026-02608-4 All-optical writing of antiferromagnetic domains using the inverse optical magnetoelectric effect in ferrotoroidic LiNiPO4 is demonstrated.
